name: Joelah
overview: Joelah was a male figure identified as the son of Jeroham from Gedor. He is noted in Scripture for coming to David at Ziklag, indicating his allegiance during a significant period in David's rise. Although his tribal affiliation is not recorded, his connection to Jeroham places him within the context of those who supported David.
namesAndTitles: The name Joelah is a proper name meaning 'let him help.' This meaning reflects a hopeful or supportive connotation, though the name itself was not given by God. The biblical reference for this name is found in 1 Chronicles 12:7.
familyAndRelationships: Joelah is explicitly identified as the son of Jeroham, as recorded in Scripture. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Joelah's significance lies in his role as one of the men who joined David at Ziklag, demonstrating loyalty to David during his time of refuge. His identification as the son of Jeroham of Gedor helps to situate him among the supporters who contributed to David's eventual establishment as king. His mention in 1 Chronicles underscores the collective support David received from various individuals and families.
